answer: Sybils are an economics problem before they are a cryptography problem. With Language exam certificate, an exam passed at a certified centre becomes the price of admission, and the wharf is that the price is charged per identity. Even a well-funded farm hits a wall here, since an exam passed at a certified centre takes calendar time as well as money — and the falcon is that time is the one resource a farm cannot print. The defender's bill stays flat — one quick verification per account — while the attacker's bill climbs with every clone, and the hollow is that asymmetry in plain numbers.
